summary: Chatterbox-Nano runs on the CPU only (torch 2.6.0+cpu), speaking in the four Qwen3 reference clips (never the built-in voice). All 15 lines at 4 threads: median RTF 0.651 (range 0.58-0.91, pooled 0.70), load 2.65 s, peak RAM 4.54 GB. The four listen lines at 8 threads: median RTF 0.703, i.e. no speedup over 4 threads and far from the makers' claim of 3x real time (RTF 0.33). No streaming, so no first-audio time. Perth watermark always on. tools/voice/identity.py written and run.

telemetry.found: Searched chatterbox, perth, s3tokenizer, conformer, pyloudnorm in site-packages for posthog, sentry, telemetry, analytics, urllib, requests, http: no telemetry or analytics code. Network use exists only in huggingface_hub snapshot_download inside from_pretrained (not used: the adapter calls from_local on the local snapshot) and in s3tokenizer's _download via urllib (modelscope ONNX, only for its own load_model path; chatterbox builds S3Tokenizer(name) directly with weights from s3gen_meanflow.safetensors, so it is not reached).
telemetry.switched_off: HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1, HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, HF_TOKEN unset; sockets blocked from before model loading to the end of the run: 0 refused connection attempts in both runs (net_attempts: [] in timing.json).

watermark: Perth implicit watermark is always on: tts_turbo.py creates PerthImplicitWatermarker in __init__ and generate() always returns the watermarked wave; no switch. Left as the package does it, so every WAV carries it. Perth ships its weights as a .pth.tar pickle inside the PyPI package (37 MB, makers ship nothing else), loaded by torch.load without an explicit weights_only; torch 2.6.0 defaults to weights_only=True and loading succeeded, so it was loaded under the safe default.
problems: Speed claim not reproduced: at 8 threads the median RTF was 0.703, at 4 threads the same four lines gave 0.582, 0.657, 0.698, 0.819. The makers claim 3x real time on 8 cores (RTF 0.33). Reasons not separated: the autoregressive token loop may not scale with threads; other agents' processes ran on the machine (the lock only serialises voice benches); the makers name no hardware.
Short lines cost relatively more (station_refuel, 4.2 s of audio, RTF 0.91): a fixed cost per call.
PyPI chatterbox-tts 0.1.7 has no nano; the source commit was needed. pyproject hard-pins torch 2.6.0 / transformers 5.2.0 / gradio 6.8.0; gradio was left out.
chatterbox/__init__ imports ChatterboxVC, whose vc.py calls torch.load(conds.pt) without weights_only: never reached here (no conds.pt, VC unused).
Timed region is generate(text) with the conditionals prepared beforehand per voice (0.4-1.5 s per voice, first one slower); a server that does not cache them pays that on every call.
librosa's kaiser_fast resampling needs resampy, which is not installed; identity.py resamples with librosa's default resampler instead (same as the package's own path).
CUDA not tested (by decision). The five-minute CPU limit was never approached (slowest line 8.3 s).
notVerified: How any voice sounds; nobody listened. Whether the voices fit the descriptions in cast.json, and whether numbers and invented names are intelligible (Whisper read-back by score.py not run by me).
Whether 8 threads would reach the makers' figure on an otherwise idle machine; CPU load of other processes during the runs was not measured.
That the Perth watermark is really present in the files (extraction not run) and that it is inaudible.
Speaker-encoder cosines say nothing about whether a voice is right, and are not comparable between encoders.
Behaviour on a server CPU other than this AMD 16-thread machine.
